NATIVE RATE INFORMATION AND RARE LIFETIMES UNDER MODEL ERROR
Root construction, continued 1 November 2026

Objective retained
==================
Predict a rare coarse-target mean lifetime and its deadline probabilities from
acquired local information, without waiting for the target event. This note
removes an exact-model restriction of the previous construction. The native
process need not have the fitted Gibbs law, preserve a known measure, or have
a supplied stationary short-cycle decomposition. It must have a justified,
bounded kinetic dependence range and the same transition support as a usable
reference. Complete native state changes and calibrated timestamps are inputs.

This is a finite theorem and an executable mathematical construction, not a
physical validation or a claim of historical priority. Count/exposure learning,
hypercontractivity, Markov potential theory and matrix perturbation are ordinary
ingredients. The addition developed here is their explicit composition into a
compact, target-uniform relative lifetime certificate for a misspecified source.
The new interface is stronger than the previous clamped/marked calibration.

All prior Astra premises are bound to
  harjassand/astra-research-knowledge
  51ce47ce39f976517d60e2f87bbe280b651f6056.
The previous proofs and source copies in this package remain unmodified.

1. Reference and actual source
=============================
Use finite row generators Q0 and Q, with L0=-Q0 and L=-Q. Both are irreducible.
The reference Q0 is executable, has known stationary probability pi0, a paid
maximum exit bound Lambda, and a paid symmetric Poincare gap g>0:
  E0(f)=<f,L0 f>_pi0 >= g Var_pi0(f).
The actual stationary probability pi is NOT an input. Suppose that native rate
confidence intervals imply the simultaneous edge bounds
  (1-eta) q0_xy <= q_xy <= (1+eta) q0_xy,       x!=y,        (1)
where 0<eta<1, and that both sources have the same off-diagonal support.
The statement is deterministic on this acquisition event.

not assumed in the explicit cube construction.

## Result: a stronger route from native observations to rare-event forecasts

I continued the same objective: **predict rare lifetimes and deadline risks in driven systems from acquired local information, without waiting for the rare event.**

The main result is now a finite transfer theorem that permits the actual process to have **an unknown stationary law and unknown stationary currents**. It connects confidence intervals for native local transition rates to relative bounds on rare mean lifetimes, then to deadline probabilities. The source no longer needs to preserve the fitted Gibbs law or the fitted stationary cycle decomposition.

I also completed a stronger 80-bit reference calculation. Its target contains \(65{,}536\) configurations, has reference probability \(2^{-64}\), and is defined by 64 parity constraints. The reference has directed pair cycles, so the convenient product-process reduction fails. The calculation uses the earlier Astra nonreversible short-excursion construction, with every proposal, null move, target preparation and membership check accounted for.

**The distinction between completed work and conditional capability is important:** the proofs, small native-history experiments and large reference calculation are complete. The high-precision native acquisition needed for the final 80-bit forecast was not executed. I derived its sufficient cost explicitly; it remains very large.

[**:chatgpt-content-reference{index="8"}**](https://chatgpt.com/library?file_id=libfile_84de72a4e95c8191b28870e342e5c6d0&account_id=personal) contains the complete work. It preserves all **66 earlier files byte-for-byte**, together with the new proofs, code, results and informative failures. The main derivation is :chatgpt-content-reference{index="9"}[REFERENCE_TRANSFER.txt](producer-workspace/REFERENCE_TRANSFER.txt); the final numerical propagation is :chatgpt-content-reference{index="10"}[driven_code_certificate.json](producer-workspace/driven_code_certificate.json).

The Astra source cutoff remains **`51ce47ce39f976517d60e2f87bbe280b651f6056`**. The corpus bindings, selected governing sources and their conditions remain in the bundle.
